Key Insights Apr 2026
🏆
Victoria record spend: $46.7B in 2025, cementing 2nd place nationally. Melbourne remains the #1 interstate overnight leisure destination with 3.5M visitors spending $5.9B.
✈️
Outbound boom: Australians took 12.4M overseas trips in 2025, forecast to surpass 13M in 2026. Average spend is AUD $9,800/trip — 15% above pre-pandemic.
🇯🇵
Japan is the standout: +24.9% YoY growth for Australian outbound travel to Japan. Strong AUD vs Yen driving interest. RACV tour partners actively promoting Japanese itineraries.
⚠️
US travel declining: September showed a -12.7% drop in Australians travelling to the USA. High airfares and cost pressures are redirecting demand to Asia. Watch RACV USA product mix.
🌏
China rebound strong: Chinese visitors to Victoria spent $3.1B, +15.4% YoY. India volume #1 nationally for VIC with $808M spend. Key inbound segments for Melbourne.
🛳️
Cruise & luxury touring up: APT, Viking, Scenic cruises all posting record bookings. RACV member segment aligns strongly with 55+ demographic driving premium travel demand.

Key Destination Trends
🌴
SE Asia dominates 2026 trending list: Vietnam, Malaysia, and the Philippines leading, driven by affordability and strong AUD/local currency rates.
❄️
"Coolcation" trend rising: Nordic/Baltic destinations (Norway, Finland, Estonia) up 20–60% YoY. Off-season Italy bookings up 166% (Intrepid data).
🏝️
Domestic standouts: Hamilton Island (#7 Google) and Lord Howe Island (#9) showing strong domestic intent. RACV resort pipeline opportunity in QLD coastal.

Aviation Developments
✈️
Qantas Project Sunrise (2026): Nonstop Sydney–New York and Sydney–London launching H2 2026. Game-changer for ultra-long-haul leisure bookings.
🍁
Qantas Vancouver–Sydney daily: Launched Jan 2026 (+68% seat increase). North America capacity up substantially — watch for RACV Canada/Alaska tour demand.
📊
Intl. passenger growth +9.5%: August 2025 vs prior year. Jetstar and Qantas top contributors. Singapore Airlines, Emirates holding strong market share.
🏙️
Domestic routes expanding: Adelaide–Melbourne, Gold Coast–Sydney, Brisbane–Melbourne all up 3–6% capacity. Good for RACV resort and domestic tour products.

Instagram: Cover-More runs destination-linked creative ("Heading to Bali? Get covered"). Allianz leverages UGC and travel influencers. RACV opportunity: tie TI creative to RACV's own destination content and resort imagery.
▶️
YouTube: Allianz runs claims-reassurance ads and destination pre-rolls. Cover-More has branded content series. RACV has minimal YouTube TI presence — opportunity to run pre-roll against travel content (Japan, Bali, Europe searches).
🔍
Comparison Sites (Finder, Canstar, Compare the Market): Cover-More and Allianz invest heavily in comparison site placement fees and sponsored positions. RACV is listed but not prominently featured. Comparison sites drive ~30–40% of category new-customer volume.
📧
Email / CRM: RACV's biggest competitive advantage — 1.7M+ member database. Competitors cannot replicate this owned audience. Cover-More relies on aggregator leads. RACV should be converting travel bookings and resort stays directly into TI upsells at point of booking.
🤝
Affiliate / Partnerships: Cover-More is embedded in airline and OTA booking flows (Qantas, Webjet). Allianz is in Webjet and Flight Centre. RACV TI could be embedded at checkout in RACV's own travel booking funnel — currently an under-exploited in-funnel placement.

Key News & Trends Impacting RACV Resorts
8 SIGNALS
⛽
Fuel crisis impact on regional travel: Remote/distant regions seeing up to −20% visitation, however proximal destinations (Mornington Peninsula, Yarra Valley, Great Ocean Road corridor) remain solid. RACV Torquay, Cape Schanck and Healesville well-positioned; Cobram more exposed.
🚌
Free VIC public transport April 2026: State government announcement creates significant day-trip and short-break opportunity for resorts within reach of Melbourne. Healesville (Yarra Valley Rail Trail) and Mornington Peninsula (via Frankston line) can activate specific campaign creative targeting non-drivers.
💰
Regional travellers spend +$286 per trip: Boomtown data shows domestic regional travellers outspend metro travellers by $286 per trip on average. RACV Resorts positioned to capture high-yield regional segments with bundled packages (golf + spa + dining).
🧖
Wellness travel boom: 58% of high-income Australians plan a wellness trip in 2026. Strong tailwind for RACV Healesville (One Spa, wine region, mountain setting) and RACV Cape Schanck (One Spa, ocean views, championship golf). Both should amplify spa + wellness messaging in paid and organic channels.
🏗️
Inverloch expansion — 36 new rooms under construction: Capacity uplift coming to RACV Inverloch. Key opportunity to pre-sell launch packages for the new room block, drive early reviews at opening, and position Inverloch as the premier coastal escape on the South Gippsland Coast.
✈️
Qantas Hobart base closure risk: Qantas network restructuring threatens air access to Hobart. RACV Hobart Hotel relies on interstate fly-in guests. Risk of reduced demand needs mitigation — drive market partnership, Tasmanian road trip packaging, and Rex/Jetstar partnerships should be explored urgently.
📶
Cobram WiFi complaint — recurring pain point: Guest reviews consistently flag no WiFi in cabins and caravan sites at RACV Cobram as a top-1 complaint. In an era of remote work and always-on connectivity, this is a booking barrier particularly for families and working travellers. Infrastructure investment recommended.
🐣
Easter 2026 results — mixed by geography: Mornington Peninsula (Cape Schanck) reported solid occupancy; remote areas (Cobram) down ~20%. Proximity to Melbourne emerging as the strongest predictor of Easter performance for RACV Resorts. Portfolio tilt toward proximal properties validates strategy.

Key Conference & Events Trends 2026
6 SIGNALS
💻
Hybrid events now standard expectation: In-person + virtual attendance is now expected for major conferences. RACV City Club's LED walls and streaming capability provide a competitive advantage. Cape Schanck and resort venues should invest in hybrid technology to capture the delegate audience beyond the physical room.
🌿
Sustainability requirements growing: Corporate event planners increasingly require carbon-neutral venue credentials, waste reduction commitments, and plant-based menu options. RACV should develop and publish a formal Event Sustainability Policy across all venues to win ESG-sensitive corporate clients.
🍷
Experiential add-ons now a decision driver: Wine tastings (Healesville), spa packages (Cape Schanck, Healesville), golf experiences (all resorts) and coastal activities (Torquay, Inverloch) are primary differentiators for corporate retreat planners choosing between venue options. RACV resorts lead on experiential breadth.
📺
Technology expectations escalating: Planners expect LED walls, real-time streaming, touch-enabled AV, app-based audience engagement and seamless WiFi across all event spaces. Venues without upgraded AV packages face deselection at shortlisting stage. Regular tech refresh cycle required.
🏞️
Regional retreat demand post-COVID structural: Corporate teams increasingly prefer off-site regional retreats over CBD venues for strategy days and leadership programs — seeking immersion, networking, and reduced digital distraction. RACV Resort network (Cape Schanck, Healesville, Torquay) uniquely positioned to capture this structural demand shift.
📊
MICE sector — $270M to Victoria in 2025: Melbourne Convention Bureau data shows 230 events secured in 2025, contributing approximately $270M to the Victorian economy. RACV's multi-venue network (CBD + regional resorts) positions it to capture both CBD MICE and regional offsite segments. MCB partnership should be formalised.
Conference & Events Watchouts
6 WATCHOUTS
City Club Parking Constraint
Limited on-site parking in CBD is a recurring objection for event planners with regional delegates.
— Amber · Ongoing friction point
RACV ACTION: Negotiate bulk parking rates with Wilson Parking or Secure Parking; partner with PT providers; create an "Event Transport Guide" for delegate packs; include tram/train access as a positive feature in sales materials.
Resort Venue Technology Gap
Resort conference facilities (Healesville, Cobram) may lack enterprise-grade hybrid AV vs CBD competitors.
— Amber · Investment required
RACV ACTION: Conduct AV audit across all resort conference facilities; prioritise LED screen and streaming upgrades at Cape Schanck and Healesville; partner with AV supplier for managed service contract across all venues.
No Formal Sustainability Policy — Events
Lack of published event sustainability credentials is a disqualifier for large corporates with ESG mandates.
▼ Red risk · Urgent for large corporates
RACV ACTION: Develop and publish an RACV Events Sustainability Policy; measure and report event carbon footprint; introduce plant-forward menu options; pursue EarthCheck or equivalent certification for event operations.
MCB Partnership Opportunity
RACV venues not prominently listed in Melbourne Convention Bureau venue directory — missed referral channel.
▲ Green opportunity · Low cost
RACV ACTION: Formalise MCB membership and venue listing; brief MCB business development team on full RACV venue network; develop a multi-venue "RACV Conference Circuit" itinerary for MCB distribution.
Regional Retreat Positioning Under-Marketed
Corporate retreat demand is structurally growing but RACV resort venues not ranked in key MICE trade publications.
▲ Green opportunity · Positioning gap
RACV ACTION: Commission a venue media shoot for all four resort conference venues; develop a dedicated "Corporate Retreats" landing page on RACV.com.au; brief Spice magazine, CIM, and MeetingsMag with content pitches; consider a hosted buyer fam trip to Cape Schanck.
No Cross-Venue Conference Package
RACV has 4 conference-capable venues but no bundled multi-venue annual conference product (city + regional).
— Amber · Revenue opportunity
RACV ACTION: Create a "RACV Conference Plus Retreat" package — AGM at City Club + leadership retreat at Cape Schanck or Healesville; price as a bundled multi-day program; target ASX200 companies with Melbourne HQs; leverage member database for direct outreach.

SWOT Analysis — RACV in Cruise Sales STRATEGIC FRAMEWORK
Strengths INTERNAL · POSITIVE
💪
2.2M member database — largest captive audience for cruise in Australia. Unmatched reach for targeted cruise offers.
🏆
Trust brand equity — 123 years, NPS +63 digital. Members trust RACV recommendations over OTA algorithms.
🤝
Curated partner portfolio — APT, Viking, Scenic, NCL, Journey Beyond covers luxury to mass market spectrum.
📊
Stacking value — RACV member discount layers on top of partner sale pricing. Unique in market, not replicable by OTAs.
📱
CRM capability — 18 always-on journeys, 1M+ portal users available for targeted cruise upsell campaigns.
🧭
In-house travel consultants — expert advice differentiates from self-serve OTA experience; critical for high-value cruise bookings.
Weaknesses INTERNAL · NEGATIVE
⚠️
No RACV-branded cruise product — selling other brands, not own-brand experience. Limited differentiation beyond member pricing.
💻
Limited online cruise booking UX — competitors Cruise1st, Cruiseable have purpose-built cruise booking experiences.
🏷️
Price perception gap — RACV associated with insurance/roadside, not "exciting cruise holidays". Brand repositioning needed.
🎯
No loyalty program integration — no RACV points on Viking, APT or Scenic bookings. Missed retention opportunity.
📋
Narrow partner portfolio — only 5 partners vs Flight Centre/Helloworld with 50+ cruise lines. Limits range of member options.
📹
Cruise content gap — no RACV cruise blog, social content, or YouTube presence. No top-of-funnel cruise content strategy.
Opportunities EXTERNAL · POSITIVE
📈
33% of Australians plan to cruise in 2026 — enormous addressable market. RACV's 2.2M members = 726K potential cruise prospects. (TTF Australia)
🧑
44% of under-35s keen on cruise — RACV can capture younger demographic via NCL and Carnival positioning. Future member pipeline.
⛽
Fuel crisis elevates cruise value — all-inclusive pricing resonates powerfully when aviation fuel surcharges hit fly-drive holidays.
🚂
Journey Beyond rail cross-sell — domestic, fuel-proof luxury alternative to aviation. Elevated positioning right now. RACV-exclusive.
🌊
Mediterranean + Kimberley demand peaks — APT and Scenic offerings perfectly timed for highest-demand cruise seasons.
🏨
RACV Resorts as cruise pre/post stay — Cape Schanck or Torquay as pre-cruise Melbourne stay package. Full end-to-end RACV journey.
Threats EXTERNAL · NEGATIVE
✈️
Jet fuel crisis — airline surcharges directly affecting fly-cruise packages which are core to APT, Viking and Scenic offerings.
📉
NCL reducing AU presence — 5 departures down from 9. Less domestic sailing inventory impacts close-to-home appeal.
🏪
OTA cruise specialists — Cruise1st, Cruiseable, Iglu Cruise growing fast with aggressive digital marketing and purpose-built cruise UX.
🏢
Flight Centre & Helloworld — broader cruise portfolios (50+ cruise lines) and larger agent distribution networks nationally.
🏛️
Overtourism in Mediterranean ports — pushback in Venice, Dubrovnik, Santorini may limit itinerary options for APT and Viking partners.
🌏
Hormuz crisis risk — may force rerouting of Middle East/Indian Ocean segments, disrupting APT Kimberley and Scenic Indian Ocean itineraries.

⛽ Fuel Crisis Context — All Cruise Segments
Fuel Crisis Opportunity Portal Banner · EDM
💬
"Skip the fuel stress — your cruise includes everything. Fly, stay, eat, explore — all one price. Your RACV membership saves you even more."
Strategic Rationale
Aviation fuel surcharges and disruption make all-inclusive cruise pricing uniquely compelling. RACV can position cruise as the rational choice — no fuel price uncertainty.
Best Partners
Viking (Fly Free stacks with cruise all-inclusive), Journey Beyond (no aviation dependency), APT (luxury all-inclusive framing aligns with value messaging).
Recommended Channels
RACV Portal homepage banner, EDM to 1M+ travel-opted members, RACV Royalauto magazine, in-branch travel consultant talking points.
🏆 Premium 55+ Demographic — APT, Viking, Scenic
Core RACV Audience Luxury Positioning
💬
"Hand-picked by RACV travel experts — intimate luxury ships, cultural enrichment, all-inclusive. From APT's Kimberley to Viking's Rhine to Scenic's Antarctica."
Strategic Rationale
RACV's core 55+ demographic trusts curation over algorithm. "Hand-picked by experts" positions RACV as advisor, not OTA. Intimate ship sizing (154–228 guests) resonates with this demographic.
Best Partners
APT (Kimberley, Mediterranean — Australian brand), Viking (Rhine, Danube — cultural enrichment), Scenic Eclipse (Antarctica, helicopter — bucket list).
Recommended Channels
Royalauto magazine (full page), RACV Travel Stores, direct mail to 55+ member segment, RACV Travel EDM drip sequence, consultant talking points.
🧑 Younger 35–44 Demographic — NCL, Close-to-Home
Growth Segment 44% Cruise Intent
💬
"1 in 3 Australians will cruise in 2026 — your RACV membership unlocks exclusive savings on Norwegian Cruise Line, with unlimited drinks, dining and WiFi included from $59/day."
Strategic Rationale
44% of under-35s now want to cruise — highest ever. NCL's close-to-home AU/NZ departures from Sydney remove barrier of flights. "$59/day" is a tangible value hook for younger price-sensitive travellers.
Best Partners
NCL Norwegian Spirit (Sydney departures, AU/NZ/Pacific), Viking entry-level ocean (14-day Europe), Journey Beyond (domestic adventure, no flights).
Recommended Channels
RACV digital channels, social media (paid META/Instagram targeting 30–44 VIC), RACV app push notification, CRM trigger on first-time travel inquiry.

Trends Impacting Attractions 5 Key Shifts
🎭 Experiential travel boom: 89% of Australians say live events make travel worthwhile. Shift from sightseeing to doing — cooking classes, wildlife encounters, artisan workshops.
🎬 Set-jetting: TV/film locations driving attraction visits (Bridgerton UK, Shogun Japan). Align content with streaming trends for attractions near filming locations.
🧘 Wellness experiences: Spa, thermal, mindfulness and nature-based experiences commanding 30%+ premium (Simon-Kucher). Yarra Valley and Cape Schanck well-positioned.
🗺️ Regional dispersal: Travellers moving beyond CBD to regional VIC. Great Ocean Road, Yarra Valley and Phillip Island benefit. Boomtown data shows +$286 regional spend premium.
🚃 VIC free public transport April 2026: Melbourne CBD attraction accessibility improves. Melbourne Skydeck and CBD experiences gain footfall without the weekday restriction impact.

Hotel & Accommodation Key Trends 5 Strategic Shifts
🏨 Accommodation-first travellers: 27% now choose destination based on accommodation. RACV resorts should lead travel inspirational content, not just support booking.
💼 Bleisure (business + leisure): Extended post-conference stays growing. RACV Royal Pines QLD positioned well for conference + leisure combination bookings.
📅 Extended stays: Average stay length increasing 20% post-pandemic. Weekly rate packages for RACV resorts with member discounts could capture this trend.
🌿 Regional short breaks: Fuel cost concerns driving proximal travel. RACV resorts within 2 hours of Melbourne (Torquay, Healesville, Cape Schanck, Inverloch) perfectly positioned.
🧖 Wellness accommodation premium: +30% price premium accepted for wellness-positioned properties (Simon-Kucher). RACV One Spa at Healesville and Cape Schanck are strategic assets.
RACV Hotel Positioning SWOT 2026
StrengthsS
✓Own resort portfolio: 6 properties, no OTA commission, full brand control and highest margin
✓Member discount: 30% off creates genuine loyalty hook vs Booking.com Genius 10%
✓VIC dominance: Melbourne #1 interstate leisure destination — RACV resorts capture that demand
✓Wellness assets: One Spa at Healesville and Cape Schanck commands +30% premium positioning
WeaknessesW
⚠Limited inventory: Only 6 resorts — interstate and international hotel coverage is weak
⚠OTA dependency: Partner hotel rates often match or exceed OTA pricing, reducing member value
⚠Digital UX gap: RACV booking experience trails Booking.com and Luxury Escapes on UX quality
⚠Urban hotel gap: No RACV-owned Melbourne CBD hotel — limits pre/post travel package potential
OpportunitiesO
▲Package ecosystem: Resort + TI + Fuel + Attraction bundle = unmatched member value proposition
▲Wellness positioning: Lean into +30% wellness premium with targeted Healesville and Cape Schanck marketing
▲Extended stay packages: Weekly deals for remote workers — bleisure at Healesville or Torquay
▲Pre/post cruise: Cape Schanck and City Club as Melbourne pre-cruise accommodation for APT/Viking passengers
ThreatsT
▼Luxury Escapes flash sales: Deep discounts on premium properties undercut RACV member pricing perception
▼Airbnb regional competition: Unique regional stays on Airbnb compete with RACV resort mid-tier rooms
▼OTA dominance: Booking.com ad spend growing — RACV hotel SEO and brand visibility at risk
▼Wage cost inflation: Hospitality labour costs squeezing resort margins despite growing demand

OTA Rate Parity Erosion
Booking.com matching or undercutting RACV partner hotel rates removes member value. Action: Audit all partner hotel rates. Negotiate exclusive member rates not available on OTAs.
Luxury Escapes Flash Sale Competition
Flash sales on comparable properties create price comparison pressure. Action: Counter with value-add packages (breakfast + spa + fuel) rather than pure price competition.
Wellness Premium Opportunity
+30% wellness accommodation premium validated by Simon-Kucher. Action: Reposition Healesville and Cape Schanck as RACV Wellness Retreats with premium package pricing.
No CBD Melbourne Property
RACV City Club is not a hotel — missing pre/post cruise Melbourne stay. Action: Negotiate preferred rate with one quality Melbourne CBD hotel for cruise + stay bundle.

Fuel Crisis — Regional Impact Analysis Active Monitor
⛽ Fuel prices averaging $2.38/L regional VIC (Apr 2025), up from $1.92 baseline. 400km+ round trip to Cobram costs $95–$120 in fuel alone for average passenger vehicle.
📉 Cobram bookings down 20% vs Easter 2024. Healesville and Inverloch showing 8–12% softness vs prior year. Mornington Peninsula resorts unaffected — within 90-min drive zone.
💡 Mitigation: "Fuel rebate" positioning for remote resorts. A $50–$80 fuel credit included in stay package removes psychological barrier at minimal cost, particularly for Cobram.
🚌 Free VIC public transport (April 2025) creates opportunity for Healesville — YVP coach from Melbourne +2hr, no fuel cost. Package a "train & stay" product to reactivate demand.

Research Synthesis — Key Implications for Resorts Strategy 3 Priority Themes
1. Wellness is the #1 growth vector
Simon-Kucher + Accor data converge: wellness travellers pay 40% more and return at 78% rate. RACV already has the spa assets — the gap is positioning and brand language, not physical investment.
2. Bundle design = RevPAR uplift
Boomtown + Salesforce data: activity-and-dining bundles seeing +34% demand; personalised pre-arrival upsell drives +17% conversion. Package design should be data-driven, not ad-hoc.
3. Awards amplification unlocks credibility
VIC Awards 2025 nominations (5 properties) are an under-used asset. Accor research: award recognition in search results increases click-through by 22%. Integrate award marks into Google listings and OTA profiles.

🧘 Wellness Premium — Members Prioritising Spa & Wellbeing Growth Trend

The global wellness economy reached $6.3 trillion in 2025 (Global Wellness Institute). In Australia, spa and wellness spending grew 19% YoY. Private club members are increasingly prioritising wellness access as a primary membership benefit — ahead of networking and dining in under-50 cohort surveys. RACV's One Spa (91% CSAT) is a genuine premium asset but currently contributes only 10% of Club revenue. Premium spa packaging — half-day retreats, couples' spa days, corporate wellness programmes — could unlock significant revenue growth.

Australian Outbound Travel — Market Overview ATIA + ABS Data

Australians made 12.4 million overseas trips in the year ending September 2025 — up 9.7% YoY and forecast to exceed 13 million in 2026. Average overseas trip spend is AUD $9,800 per trip, 15% above pre-pandemic levels, driven by longer trip durations and premium experience preference.

Market size: The Australian cruise market is valued at $237M (GBV) growing at 10% CAGR. River cruise is the fastest-growing segment (+18% CAGR) driven by European demand from 55+ Australians.

33% plan to cruise: ATIA data shows 33% of Australians are planning a cruise holiday in the next 24 months — the highest intent since pre-pandemic. RACV's cruise portfolio is well-positioned to capture this demand.
🌊
Expedition surge: Expedition cruising (Antarctica, Arctic, Kimberley) grew 70% in FY25. Scenic Eclipse, Silversea, APT Seabourn all reporting full ships. RACV should increase expedition product marketing.

Tour Market Trends
🚌
Small group dominates: Small-group touring (8–16 passengers) is outgrowing large coach (40+) by 3:1 in premium segment. Intrepid, APT and G Adventures all posting record demand. RACV's partner mix is well-aligned.
🌱
Sustainable travel premium: 58% of Australian travellers say sustainability influences their booking decisions (Intrepid/ATIA 2025). B Corp status and low-impact itineraries command 10–15% price premium.
🇦🇺
Domestic touring resurgence: Australian domestic tours grew 18% in FY25 driven by Kimberley, Outback and Tasmania demand. RACV's Spirit of Tasmania, Ghan and World Expeditions partnerships are directly on trend.
Experience Economy — $213B Global
💎
Experiences over things: The global experience economy reached $213B in 2025. Australians rank 4th globally for per-capita experience spending. Travel experiences are the #1 discretionary spend category for 45+ Australians.
👴
Silver economy surge: 65+ Australians represent 17% of population but 31% of premium travel spend. RACV's membership skews to this cohort — a structural competitive advantage as this demographic grows.
🏔️
Coolcation trend: Nordic destinations — Iceland, Norway, Greenland — are up 45% for Australian bookings as travellers seek cooler, less-crowded alternatives to traditional hotspots. Monitor Viking & Ponant Arctic product.

RACV travel consultants should proactively contact affected members booked on Middle East segments and assist with itinerary change management.

Expedia, Booking.com and Google have all launched AI trip-planning assistants in Q1 2026. Early data shows AI-assisted bookings converting at 2.3x the rate of standard search. This is a structural threat to the traditional travel agent model. RACV Travel's human-expert positioning ("our consultants know which tour is right for you") is the key differentiation — this messaging should be strengthened in all consumer communications this quarter.

🤖
RACV response: Invest in AI-assisted trip planning on racv.com.au — but position it as "AI + human expert review" to maintain trust advantage over pure-OTA competitors. Pilot with cruise product first.

Benefits News — April/May 2026 5 Stories
⛽
Fuel Savings May 2026
RACV Members Save Record $1.8 Million at the Bowser

RACV members have collectively saved $1.8 million in fuel costs across April and May 2026, the highest single-period saving in the fuel discount program's history. The record is driven by exceptional fuel price volatility, with Melbourne average unleaded prices reaching 178.4c/L — near cycle peak — meaning the 5c/L RACV discount delivers proportionally greater absolute savings. Usage of the program surged 24% as price-sensitive members actively sought out participating stations.

💡 Marketing opportunity: Deploy email + push campaign highlighting $1.8M headline. "Your 5c saves bigger when prices are highest" — direct CoL messaging to re-engage lapsed fuel discount users.

Source: RACV Member Benefits · Analytics May 2026

📉
Fuel Policy Apr 2026
Federal Excise Cut 26.3c/L Passed Through — Price Relief Short-Lived

The federal government's excise halving measure delivered a 26.3c/L cut at the pump from early April 2026 — the largest single government-mandated fuel price intervention in Australia's history. However, analysts warn the relief was already being eroded within 3 weeks as global oil prices and refinery margins reasserted. RACT and NRMA have both issued public statements calling for the measure to be extended. RACV's 5c/L discount compounds the benefit, giving members a combined saving of up to 31.3c/L at the peak of relief.

💡 Timing signal: Monitor price bounce-back closely. When prices recover above 170c/L, re-activate "5c makes the difference" messaging across social and EDM channels.

Source: ACCC Petrol Monitor Apr 2026

🚫
Supply Alert Apr 3, 2026
81 Victorian Petrol Stations Run Dry — Supply Chain Disruption

A logistics disruption at the Geelong refinery and downstream distribution network caused 81 Victorian petrol stations to run out of fuel on April 3, 2026 — the largest domestic fuel stockout event since 2022. The event lasted 18–36 hours and disproportionately affected outer suburban and regional areas. RACV Roadside received a 34% spike in calls related to fuel and breakdown on the day. The RACV fuel discount network's real-time station availability data proved critical, with the RACV app recording its highest single-day traffic in 3 years as members checked live availability.

💡 Value demonstration: The April 3 event demonstrated the value of RACV's live station availability feature. Amplify this capability in acquisition messaging — "Know before you go: RACV app shows live fuel availability at 700+ stations."

Source: RACV Fuel Hub · Internal Ops data Apr 3 2026

🔋
EV Apr 2026
RACV EV Charging Network Grows to 142 Sites — 328,000 EVs on VIC Roads

Victoria's EV fleet has reached 328,000 registered electric vehicles, representing 12.4% of new vehicle sales and growing 58% year-on-year. RACV's own EV charging network expanded to 142 charge points in Q1 2026, adding 24 new sites, predominantly along freeway corridors and at destination retail precincts. Session volumes are up 38% YoY. The 10% RACV member charging discount is increasingly becoming a consideration factor in new EV purchase decisions, per internal member research.

💡 Acquisition hook: Target the 328K VIC EV owners who are not yet RACV members. Messaging: "Save 10% every charge. RACV EV charging discount + 142 locations statewide." Direct digital targeting via EV owner social communities and EV forum platforms.

Source: RACV Electric Vehicles · VicRoads EV Registration Data Apr 2026

🚌
Transport Policy Apr 2026
Free VIC Public Transport — April Holiday Period Reduces Private Car Dependence

The Victorian Government's free public transport initiative during the April school holiday period (April 12–27, 2026) reduced private vehicle trips into Melbourne's CBD by an estimated 18% over the period. While this temporarily dampened fuel discount usage in the inner-suburban member cohort, outer suburban and regional members saw no change in fuel demand. RACV's motoring advocacy team notes the policy as consistent with long-term modal shift goals, while maintaining that private vehicle ownership and the associated member benefits remain essential for Victoria's suburban and regional majority.

💡 Context note: Free PT events are temporary. Outer suburban members (60%+ of base) remain unaffected. Use inter-period fuel savings data to counter any narrative that "driving is declining" — suburban/regional members drive more, not less, than 5 years ago.

Source: Transport for Victoria Apr 2026

Strategic Takeaways — What RACV Must Do Now Synthesised from competitor analysis
🥇 Copy Cover-More's content architecture: Build dedicated destination pages (20+), product landing pages (cruise, seniors, family), and deep FAQ libraries. Cover-More's dominance is 70% content volume, 30% brand. RACV can replicate the structure without replicating the brand.
🔬 Copy Allianz's data strategy: Publish an annual "RACV Travel Insurance Insights Report" with claims data, popular destinations, average premiums. This single asset would be cited by AI more than any other content type. Allianz's research drives ~30% of their AI citations.
👴 Steal Southern Cross's niche: Southern Cross is cited for seniors because of one dedicated page. RACV covers to age 110 vs Southern Cross's no-age-limit positioning. A single well-optimised seniors page with schema markup would directly compete for Southern Cross's most valuable AI citations.
📋 Copy 1Cover's FAQ density: 1Cover wins AI citations disproportionate to their brand size because of their high-density FAQ architecture. Every product page has 15+ FAQs with FAQPage schema. RACV should implement this on all existing pages immediately — it's low-effort, high-impact.
🏥 Copy Bupa's authority signalling: Bupa leverages its health brand for travel insurance authority. RACV should leverage its 123-year motoring and member service heritage, RACV roadside assistance trust, and safety expertise as equivalent authority signals. The RACV brand is more trusted in Victoria than Bupa — use it.
🔗 Invest in comparison site domination: All 5 competitors have stronger Finder/Canstar/Compare the Market presences than RACV. Being listed is not enough — RACV needs to be "Editor's Choice" or "Best For Seniors" on at least 2 comparison sites. These citations cascade directly into AI engine responses.
